## Built your Android app with Claude Code? Get your 12 testers for 14 days
URL: https://testerexchange.com/guide/get-12-testers-claude-code/

Claude Code can write and build your Android app, but it cannot supply the 12 real testers Google Play requires. If your personal developer account was created after 13 November 2023, you must run a closed test with at least 12 testers opted in for 14 continuous days before applying for production. This guide covers building the bundle, starting closed testing, getting the testers (free first, paid second) and connecting Tester Exchange to Claude Code so the agent can do the paperwork.

### 1. Build the release bundle (.aab)

1. Ask Claude Code to configure release signing in your module's build.gradle.kts (a signingConfigs block with storeFile, storePassword, keyAlias and keyPassword, set on the release build type). Keep passwords out of git (Android's build docs: https://developer.android.com/build/building-cmdline).
2. Run ./gradlew bundleRelease in the terminal. Gradle builds and signs the bundle; the .aab normally appears under app/build/outputs/bundle/release/, but check your own build output.
3. Create a keystore with keytool if you don't have one, and back it up. Google Play App Signing is offered when you upload your first release.

### 2. Start closed testing in Play Console

1. Open Test and release > Testing > Closed testing, then Create track (or Manage track).
2. Click Create new release, upload the .aab, add a release name and notes, Save as draft, Next, then Start rollout (steps from https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9859348).
3. Complete the app setup tasks on the Dashboard first, or the release button stays disabled.

### 3. Get your 12 testers: free first, paid second

- Free route: open https://testerexchange.com/earn on your phone and test the apps you are given. Each app you test brings a tester to yours.
- Paid route: pay once and testers are assigned automatically. Current prices are listed at https://testerexchange.com/llms.txt.
- Ask for 15 testers rather than 12 so one dropout can't leave you under Google's minimum.

### 4. Connect Tester Exchange to Claude Code (optional)

First create an API key at https://testerexchange.com/api. Then run this once in your terminal, replacing tx_YOUR_TOKEN with your key (the command is the one listed at https://testerexchange.com/agents/):

claude mcp add --transport http tester-exchange https://vvrlxzbngxfxddywidoq.supabase.co/functions/v1/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer tx_YOUR_TOKEN"

The server is plain MCP over Streamable HTTP without OAuth; the public tools (about, pricing, platform_stats) work without a key. Keep the key out of git and out of shared config files.

### 5. Ask Claude Code

- "Use Tester Exchange to get 15 testers for com.example.app and tell me what I must do in Play Console."
- "Check my Tester Exchange campaign for com.example.app and tell me how many testers were active yesterday."
- "Pull the campaign report and draft my production access answers from the real numbers."

The main tool is get_testers: it adds the app, opens its test and returns the steps only a human can do, such as adding the testers' Google Group in Play Console. The agent cannot pay or click Apply for production for you.

### No MCP? Use the HTTP API

POST https://vvrlxzbngxfxddywidoq.supabase.co/rest/v1/rpc/agent_call with the public apikey header listed at https://testerexchange.com/agents/ and the body {"p_token":"tx_YOUR_TOKEN","p_action":"get_testers","p_args":{"package_name":"com.example.app"}}. The schema is at https://testerexchange.com/openapi.json. More tools: https://testerexchange.com/guide/ai-builders/.

### Frequently asked questions

**Can Claude Code complete the 14-day test for me?** No. The 14 days need real people using your app on their own Android phones. Claude Code can build the app and drive the setup.

**Is Tester Exchange an official Claude Code integration?** No. It is an independent service that works with any client supporting remote MCP over HTTP, which Claude Code does.

**Where does the AAB go?** Upload it to a closed testing release in Play Console, then add your testers' Google Group or email list on that track.

**Is there a free way to get the 12 testers?** Yes. Test other developers' apps at https://testerexchange.com/earn; each app you test brings a tester to yours.

---

## Built your Android app with Cursor? Get your 12 testers for 14 days
URL: https://testerexchange.com/guide/get-12-testers-cursor/

Cursor can write and build your Android app, but it cannot supply the 12 real testers Google Play requires. If your personal developer account was created after 13 November 2023, you must run a closed test with at least 12 testers opted in for 14 continuous days before applying for production. This guide covers building the bundle, starting closed testing, getting the testers (free first, paid second) and connecting Tester Exchange to Cursor so the agent can do the paperwork.

### 1. Build the release bundle (.aab)

1. Ask Cursor's agent to configure release signing in your module's build.gradle.kts (a signingConfigs block with storeFile, storePassword, keyAlias and keyPassword, set on the release build type). Keep passwords out of git (Android's build docs: https://developer.android.com/build/building-cmdline).
2. Run ./gradlew bundleRelease in the terminal. Gradle builds and signs the bundle; the .aab normally appears under app/build/outputs/bundle/release/, but check your own build output.
3. Create a keystore with keytool if you don't have one, and back it up. Google Play App Signing is offered when you upload your first release.

### 2. Start closed testing in Play Console

1. Open Test and release > Testing > Closed testing, then Create track (or Manage track).
2. Click Create new release, upload the .aab, add a release name and notes, Save as draft, Next, then Start rollout (steps from https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9859348).

### 4. Connect Tester Exchange to Cursor (optional)

First create an API key at https://testerexchange.com/api. Then put this in .cursor/mcp.json in your project, or in ~/.cursor/mcp.json to use it everywhere (file locations from Cursor's MCP docs, https://cursor.com/docs/context/mcp). Set TESTER_EXCHANGE_KEY in your shell environment first, so the key is not committed:

{"mcpServers":{"tester-exchange":{"url":"https://vvrlxzbngxfxddywidoq.supabase.co/functions/v1/mcp","headers":{"Authorization":"Bearer ${env:TESTER_EXCHANGE_KEY}"}}}}

Cursor resolves ${env:NAME} in the url and headers fields. If a server fails to load, open the Output panel and choose MCP Logs. The server is plain MCP over Streamable HTTP without OAuth; the public tools (about, pricing, platform_stats) work without a key.

### 5. Ask the agent

- "Use Tester Exchange to get 15 testers for com.example.app and tell me what I must do in Play Console."
- "Check my Tester Exchange campaign for com.example.app and tell me how many testers were active yesterday."
- "Pull the campaign report and draft my production access answers from the real numbers."

The main tool is get_testers: it adds the app, opens its test and returns the steps only a human can do, such as adding the testers' Google Group in Play Console. The agent cannot pay or click Apply for production for you.

### No MCP? Use the HTTP API

POST https://vvrlxzbngxfxddywidoq.supabase.co/rest/v1/rpc/agent_call with the public apikey header listed at https://testerexchange.com/agents/ and the body {"p_token":"tx_YOUR_TOKEN","p_action":"get_testers","p_args":{"package_name":"com.example.app"}}. The schema is at https://testerexchange.com/openapi.json. More tools: https://testerexchange.com/guide/ai-builders/.

### Frequently asked questions

**Can Cursor complete the 14-day test for me?** No. The 14 days need real people using your app on their own Android phones. Cursor can build the app and drive the setup.

**Is Tester Exchange an official Cursor integration?** No. It is an independent service that works with any client supporting remote MCP over HTTP, which Cursor does.

**Where does the AAB go?** Upload it to a closed testing release in Play Console, then add your testers' Google Group or email list on that track.

**Is there a free way to get the 12 testers?** Yes. Test other developers' apps at https://testerexchange.com/earn; each app you test brings a tester to yours.

## Emergent: publish on Google Play and get your 12 testers
URL: https://testerexchange.com/guide/get-12-testers-emergent/

Short answer: Emergent does not skip Google's rule. Emergent can produce web apps and mobile apps. Look at the code it gives you: a web project is wrapped with Capacitor, an Expo project is built with EAS Build. Either way the end result you upload to Google Play is a signed .aab file. Then your account needs 12 testers opted in for 14 days in a row before you can apply for production. This guide covers the path in order and includes a prompt you can paste into your AI assistant.

### From Emergent to Google Play

Emergent can produce web apps and mobile apps. Look at the code it gives you: a web project is wrapped with Capacitor, an Expo project is built with EAS Build. Either way the end result you upload to Google Play is a signed .aab file.

What Emergent gives you is a web or mobile project. Google Play only takes a signed Android App Bundle (.aab), so the work is getting from one to the other. Features and export options of any builder change often, so check Emergent's current documentation for your plan.

### Wrap the web app with Capacitor

Capacitor is an open-source runtime that loads your built web files inside an Android app. The AI prompt below asks your builder (or any coding assistant) to set it up.

1. Get the project code out of Emergent (GitHub sync or download) and open it on your computer. Install Node.js and Android Studio.
2. Choose an application ID like com.yourname.yourapp. It must be unique and it can never be changed after you upload to Google Play.
3. Run npx cap add android once, then npx cap sync android after every web build.
4. Open the Android project (npx cap open android) and create a signing key in Android Studio: Build, Generate Signed Bundle / APK, Android App Bundle. Keep the key file and passwords safe; you need them for every update.
5. Test the .aab on a real phone before you upload it.

Give the app something a plain website does not: working offline pages, native share, notifications or at least a good mobile layout and a real purpose. Google can reject apps that only repackage a website without added value.

### Run the closed test: 12 testers for 14 days

Google requires personal developer accounts created after 13 November 2023 to run a closed test with at least 12 testers who stay opted in for 14 days in a row before they can apply for production access. The requirement is the same whatever tool built Emergent app.

1. In Play Console, create the app (name, default language, app or game, free or paid) and fill in the declarations Google asks for.
2. Open Test and release, then Testing, then Closed testing. Create a release and upload your signed .aab file.
3. Under Testers, add an email list or a Google Group. If you use Tester Exchange, the group to add is testerexchange-testers@googlegroups.com and we add our testers to it.
4. Check Countries / regions includes the countries your testers live in.
5. Send the release for review. When the app status is Published, share the opt-in link; each tester must open it and accept.
6. Keep at least 12 testers opted in for 14 consecutive days. Aim for 15 so one dropout does not move your date.
7. When the Dashboard shows the Apply for production button, apply and answer the three parts of the form.

No friends with Android phones? Tester Exchange gives you real people on their own phones, each day they open your app is recorded, and dropouts are replaced. You can also test other developers' apps free at https://testerexchange.com/earn and each app you test brings a tester to yours.

### Common mistakes

- Do not use the Play Console "internal testing" track for the 12-tester requirement. It has to be a closed (or equivalent) test with 12 testers opted in.
- Do not change the application ID after the first upload. A new ID is a new app and restarts the 14 days.
- Do not hand testers a debug build or an .apk. Upload a signed .aab to the track so testers install from Google Play.
- Make sure the app does real work on first launch. Testers who see a blank page or login wall they cannot pass will not keep using it.
- Plan for 15 testers, not 12: dropouts before day 14 push the date back.

### Frequently asked questions

**Can I publish a Emergent app on Google Play?** Yes, once you have a signed Android App Bundle (.aab). Emergent can produce web apps and mobile apps. Look at the code it gives you: a web project is wrapped with Capacitor, an Expo project is built with EAS Build. Either way the end result you upload to Google Play is a signed .aab file.

**Does Emergent get me the 12 testers?** No. The 12 testers are a Google Play requirement for new personal developer accounts, so you recruit them yourself or use a service. Tester Exchange provides real people on their own phones, or you can swap tests for free.

**Do I need a new Play Console account for an AI-built app?** No. Google Play does not care which tool wrote the code. What matters is the account type: personal accounts created after 13 November 2023 need the 12-tester, 14-day closed test; organization accounts are not subject to that requirement.

**Can the testers be the same for several apps?** Testers opt in per app. A person can test several of your apps, but each person has to opt in to each app separately.

---

## Expo: publish on Google Play and get your 12 testers
URL: https://testerexchange.com/guide/get-12-testers-expo/

Short answer: Expo does not skip Google's rule. Expo apps are built into an Android App Bundle with EAS Build. Expo says to create the first release in Play Console yourself; later builds can be submitted from the command line. Then your account needs 12 testers opted in for 14 days in a row before you can apply for production. This guide covers the path in order and includes a prompt you can paste into your AI assistant.

### From Expo to Google Play

Expo apps are built into an Android App Bundle with EAS Build. Expo says to create the first release in Play Console yourself; later builds can be submitted from the command line.

What Expo gives you is a React Native project. Google Play only takes a signed Android App Bundle (.aab), so the work is getting from one to the other. Features and export options of any builder change often, so check Expo's current documentation for your plan.

### Build the .aab with EAS

1. Set a unique android.package in app.json (for example com.yourname.yourapp). It cannot change after you upload.
2. Make sure eas.json has a production profile that builds an app bundle.
3. Run eas build --platform android --profile production. EAS can create and store the signing key for you.
4. Download the .aab. Create the app in Play Console and upload this first build by hand to the closed testing track, as the Expo docs describe.
5. For later updates you can use eas submit, with a Google service account key.

### Run the closed test: 12 testers for 14 days

Google requires personal developer accounts created after 13 November 2023 to run a closed test with at least 12 testers who stay opted in for 14 days in a row before they can apply for production access. The requirement is the same whatever tool built Expo app.

1. In Play Console, create the app (name, default language, app or game, free or paid) and fill in the declarations Google asks for.
2. Open Test and release, then Testing, then Closed testing. Create a release and upload your signed .aab file.
3. Under Testers, add an email list or a Google Group. If you use Tester Exchange, the group to add is testerexchange-testers@googlegroups.com and we add our testers to it.
4. Check Countries / regions includes the countries your testers live in.
5. Send the release for review. When the app status is Published, share the opt-in link; each tester must open it and accept.
6. Keep at least 12 testers opted in for 14 consecutive days. Aim for 15 so one dropout does not move your date.
7. When the Dashboard shows the Apply for production button, apply and answer the three parts of the form.

No friends with Android phones? Tester Exchange gives you real people on their own phones, each day they open your app is recorded, and dropouts are replaced. You can also test other developers' apps free at https://testerexchange.com/earn and each app you test brings a tester to yours.

### Common mistakes

- Do not use the Play Console "internal testing" track for the 12-tester requirement. It has to be a closed (or equivalent) test with 12 testers opted in.
- Do not change the application ID after the first upload. A new ID is a new app and restarts the 14 days.
- Do not hand testers a debug build or an .apk. Upload a signed .aab to the track so testers install from Google Play.
- Make sure the app does real work on first launch. Testers who see a blank page or login wall they cannot pass will not keep using it.
- Plan for 15 testers, not 12: dropouts before day 14 push the date back.

### Frequently asked questions

**Can I publish a Expo app on Google Play?** Yes, once you have a signed Android App Bundle (.aab). Expo apps are built into an Android App Bundle with EAS Build. Expo says to create the first release in Play Console yourself; later builds can be submitted from the command line.

**Does Expo get me the 12 testers?** No. The 12 testers are a Google Play requirement for new personal developer accounts, so you recruit them yourself or use a service. Tester Exchange provides real people on their own phones, or you can swap tests for free.

**Do I need a new Play Console account for an AI-built app?** No. Google Play does not care which tool wrote the code. What matters is the account type: personal accounts created after 13 November 2023 need the 12-tester, 14-day closed test; organization accounts are not subject to that requirement.

**Can the testers be the same for several apps?** Testers opt in per app. A person can test several of your apps, but each person has to opt in to each app separately.

## FlutterFlow: publish on Google Play and get your 12 testers
URL: https://testerexchange.com/guide/get-12-testers-flutterflow/

Short answer: FlutterFlow does not skip Google's rule. FlutterFlow generates a real Flutter app, so you do not need a wrapper. FlutterFlow can build the Android release for you, or you can download the code and build it with the Flutter tool. Then your account needs 12 testers opted in for 14 days in a row before you can apply for production. This guide covers the path in order and includes a prompt you can paste into your AI assistant.

### From FlutterFlow to Google Play

FlutterFlow generates a real Flutter app, so you do not need a wrapper. FlutterFlow can build the Android release for you, or you can download the code and build it with the Flutter tool.

What FlutterFlow gives you is a Flutter app. Google Play only takes a signed Android App Bundle (.aab), so the work is getting from one to the other. Features and export options of any builder change often, so check FlutterFlow's current documentation for your plan.

### Produce the signed .aab

1. Open your project settings and set the app name, a unique package name (for example com.yourname.yourapp), the icon and the version and build number. The package name cannot change after you upload.
2. Use FlutterFlow's deploy options to build the Android release, or download the code and run flutter build appbundle.
3. Let Google Play App Signing manage the final key when Play Console offers it, and keep your upload key safe.
4. Install the build on a real phone and check the main flows.
5. Create the app in Play Console and upload the .aab to a closed testing track.

### Run the closed test: 12 testers for 14 days

Google requires personal developer accounts created after 13 November 2023 to run a closed test with at least 12 testers who stay opted in for 14 days in a row before they can apply for production access. The requirement is the same whatever tool built FlutterFlow app.

1. In Play Console, create the app (name, default language, app or game, free or paid) and fill in the declarations Google asks for.
2. Open Test and release, then Testing, then Closed testing. Create a release and upload your signed .aab file.
3. Under Testers, add an email list or a Google Group. If you use Tester Exchange, the group to add is testerexchange-testers@googlegroups.com and we add our testers to it.
4. Check Countries / regions includes the countries your testers live in.
5. Send the release for review. When the app status is Published, share the opt-in link; each tester must open it and accept.
6. Keep at least 12 testers opted in for 14 consecutive days. Aim for 15 so one dropout does not move your date.
7. When the Dashboard shows the Apply for production button, apply and answer the three parts of the form.

No friends with Android phones? Tester Exchange gives you real people on their own phones, each day they open your app is recorded, and dropouts are replaced. You can also test other developers' apps free at https://testerexchange.com/earn and each app you test brings a tester to yours.

### Common mistakes

- Do not use the Play Console "internal testing" track for the 12-tester requirement. It has to be a closed (or equivalent) test with 12 testers opted in.
- Do not change the application ID after the first upload. A new ID is a new app and restarts the 14 days.
- Do not hand testers a debug build or an .apk. Upload a signed .aab to the track so testers install from Google Play.
- Make sure the app does real work on first launch. Testers who see a blank page or login wall they cannot pass will not keep using it.
- Plan for 15 testers, not 12: dropouts before day 14 push the date back.

### Frequently asked questions

**Can I publish a FlutterFlow app on Google Play?** Yes, once you have a signed Android App Bundle (.aab). FlutterFlow generates a real Flutter app, so you do not need a wrapper. FlutterFlow can build the Android release for you, or you can download the code and build it with the Flutter tool.

**Does FlutterFlow get me the 12 testers?** No. The 12 testers are a Google Play requirement for new personal developer accounts, so you recruit them yourself or use a service. Tester Exchange provides real people on their own phones, or you can swap tests for free.

**Do I need a new Play Console account for an AI-built app?** No. Google Play does not care which tool wrote the code. What matters is the account type: personal accounts created after 13 November 2023 need the 12-tester, 14-day closed test; organization accounts are not subject to that requirement.

**Can the testers be the same for several apps?** Testers opt in per app. A person can test several of your apps, but each person has to opt in to each app separately.

## Built your Android app with Gemini CLI? Get your 12 testers for 14 days
URL: https://testerexchange.com/guide/get-12-testers-gemini-cli/

Gemini CLI can write and build your Android app, but it cannot supply the 12 real testers Google Play requires. If your personal developer account was created after 13 November 2023, you must run a closed test with at least 12 testers opted in for 14 continuous days before applying for production. This guide covers building the bundle, starting closed testing, getting the testers (free first, paid second) and connecting Tester Exchange to Gemini CLI so the agent can do the paperwork.

### 1. Build the release bundle (.aab)

1. Ask Gemini CLI to configure release signing in your module's build.gradle.kts (a signingConfigs block with storeFile, storePassword, keyAlias and keyPassword, set on the release build type). Keep passwords out of git (Android's build docs: https://developer.android.com/build/building-cmdline).
2. Run ./gradlew bundleRelease in the terminal. Gradle builds and signs the bundle; the .aab normally appears under app/build/outputs/bundle/release/, but check your own build output.
3. Create a keystore with keytool if you don't have one, and back it up. Google Play App Signing is offered when you upload your first release.

### 2. Start closed testing in Play Console

1. Open Test and release > Testing > Closed testing, then Create track (or Manage track).
2. Click Create new release, upload the .aab, add a release name and notes, Save as draft, Next, then Start rollout (steps from https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9859348).
3. Complete the app setup tasks on the Dashboard first, or the release button stays disabled.

### 3. Get your 12 testers: free first, paid second

- Free route: open https://testerexchange.com/earn on your phone and test the apps you are given. Each app you test brings a tester to yours.
- Paid route: pay once and testers are assigned automatically. Current prices are listed at https://testerexchange.com/llms.txt.
- Ask for 15 testers rather than 12 so one dropout can't leave you under Google's minimum.

### 4. Connect Tester Exchange to Gemini CLI (optional)

First create an API key at https://testerexchange.com/api. Then run this once in your terminal, replacing tx_YOUR_TOKEN with your key (the command is the one listed at https://testerexchange.com/agents/):

gemini mcp add --transport http tester-exchange https://vvrlxzbngxfxddywidoq.supabase.co/functions/v1/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer tx_YOUR_TOKEN"

The server is plain MCP over Streamable HTTP without OAuth; the public tools (about, pricing, platform_stats) work without a key. Keep the key out of git and out of shared config files.

### 5. Ask the agent

- "Use Tester Exchange to get 15 testers for com.example.app and tell me what I must do in Play Console."
- "Check my Tester Exchange campaign for com.example.app and tell me how many testers were active yesterday."
- "Pull the campaign report and draft my production access answers from the real numbers."

The main tool is get_testers: it adds the app, opens its test and returns the steps only a human can do, such as adding the testers' Google Group in Play Console. The agent cannot pay or click Apply for production for you.

### No MCP? Use the HTTP API

POST https://vvrlxzbngxfxddywidoq.supabase.co/rest/v1/rpc/agent_call with the public apikey header listed at https://testerexchange.com/agents/ and the body {"p_token":"tx_YOUR_TOKEN","p_action":"get_testers","p_args":{"package_name":"com.example.app"}}. The schema is at https://testerexchange.com/openapi.json. More tools: https://testerexchange.com/guide/ai-builders/.

### Frequently asked questions

**Can Gemini CLI complete the 14-day test for me?** No. The 14 days need real people using your app on their own Android phones. Gemini CLI can build the app and drive the setup.

**Is Tester Exchange an official Gemini CLI integration?** No. It is an independent service that works with any client supporting remote MCP over HTTP, which Gemini CLI does.

**Where does the AAB go?** Upload it to a closed testing release in Play Console, then add your testers' Google Group or email list on that track.

**Is there a free way to get the 12 testers?** Yes. Test other developers' apps at https://testerexchange.com/earn; each app you test brings a tester to yours.

---

3. Under Testers, add an email list or a Google Group. If you use Tester Exchange, the group to add is testerexchange-testers@googlegroups.com and we add our testers to it.
4. Check Countries / regions includes the countries your testers live in.
5. Send the release for review. When the app status is Published, share the opt-in link; each tester must open it and accept.
6. Keep at least 12 testers opted in for 14 consecutive days. Aim for 15 so one dropout does not move your date.
7. When the Dashboard shows the Apply for production button, apply and answer the three parts of the form.

No friends with Android phones? Tester Exchange gives you real people on their own phones, each day they open your app is recorded, and dropouts are replaced. You can also test other developers' apps free at https://testerexchange.com/earn and each app you test brings a tester to yours.

### Common mistakes

- Do not use the Play Console "internal testing" track for the 12-tester requirement. It has to be a closed (or equivalent) test with 12 testers opted in.
- Do not change the application ID after the first upload. A new ID is a new app and restarts the 14 days.
- Do not hand testers a debug build or an .apk. Upload a signed .aab to the track so testers install from Google Play.
- Make sure the app does real work on first launch. Testers who see a blank page or login wall they cannot pass will not keep using it.
- Plan for 15 testers, not 12: dropouts before day 14 push the date back.

### Frequently asked questions

**Can I publish a Replit app on Google Play?** Yes, once you have a signed Android App Bundle (.aab). Replit projects can be web apps or Expo (React Native) mobile apps. A web app is wrapped with Capacitor; an Expo app is built into an .aab with EAS Build. Look at the project files to see which one you have.

**Does Replit get me the 12 testers?** No. The 12 testers are a Google Play requirement for new personal developer accounts, so you recruit them yourself or use a service. Tester Exchange provides real people on their own phones, or you can swap tests for free.

**Do I need a new Play Console account for an AI-built app?** No. Google Play does not care which tool wrote the code. What matters is the account type: personal accounts created after 13 November 2023 need the 12-tester, 14-day closed test; organization accounts are not subject to that requirement.

**Can the testers be the same for several apps?** Testers opt in per app. A person can test several of your apps, but each person has to opt in to each app separately.

---

## Built your Android app with VS Code + Copilot? Get your 12 testers for 14 days
URL: https://testerexchange.com/guide/get-12-testers-vscode-copilot/

VS Code + Copilot can write and build your Android app, but it cannot supply the 12 real testers Google Play requires. If your personal developer account was created after 13 November 2023, you must run a closed test with at least 12 testers opted in for 14 continuous days before applying for production. This guide covers building the bundle, starting closed testing, getting the testers (free first, paid second) and connecting Tester Exchange to VS Code + Copilot so the agent can do the paperwork.

### 1. Build the release bundle (.aab)

1. Ask VS Code + Copilot's agent to configure release signing in your module's build.gradle.kts (a signingConfigs block with storeFile, storePassword, keyAlias and keyPassword, set on the release build type). Keep passwords out of git (Android's build docs: https://developer.android.com/build/building-cmdline).
2. Run ./gradlew bundleRelease in the terminal. Gradle builds and signs the bundle; the .aab normally appears under app/build/outputs/bundle/release/, but check your own build output.
3. Create a keystore with keytool if you don't have one, and back it up. Google Play App Signing is offered when you upload your first release.

### 2. Start closed testing in Play Console

1. Open Test and release > Testing > Closed testing, then Create track (or Manage track).
2. Click Create new release, upload the .aab, add a release name and notes, Save as draft, Next, then Start rollout (steps from https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9859348).
3. Complete the app setup tasks on the Dashboard first, or the release button stays disabled.

### 3. Get your 12 testers: free first, paid second

- Free route: open https://testerexchange.com/earn on your phone and test the apps you are given. Each app you test brings a tester to yours.
- Paid route: pay once and testers are assigned automatically. Current prices are listed at https://testerexchange.com/llms.txt.
- Ask for 15 testers rather than 12 so one dropout can't leave you under Google's minimum.

### 4. Connect Tester Exchange to VS Code + Copilot (optional)

First create an API key at https://testerexchange.com/api. Then create .vscode/mcp.json in your project (or use the mcp.json in your VS Code user profile for all projects) with the config below, the "servers" format listed at https://testerexchange.com/agents/. The "inputs" entry makes VS Code ask for your key in a password prompt, so it is not written into the file or committed to git (VS Code's MCP docs: https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/customization/mcp-servers):

{"inputs":[{"type":"promptString","id":"tx-key","description":"Tester Exchange API key (tx_...)","password":true}],"servers":{"tester-exchange":{"type":"http","url":"https://vvrlxzbngxfxddywidoq.supabase.co/functions/v1/mcp","headers":{"Authorization":"Bearer ${input:tx-key}"}}}}

Paste your tx_ key when VS Code asks. Copilot chooses the relevant tools itself and asks you to approve them as they appear; manage servers through Chat: Open Customizations > MCP Servers. An organisation policy can block MCP servers. The server is plain MCP over Streamable HTTP without OAuth; the public tools (about, pricing, platform_stats) work without a key.

### 5. Ask the agent

- "Use Tester Exchange to get 15 testers for com.example.app and tell me what I must do in Play Console."
- "Check my Tester Exchange campaign for com.example.app and tell me how many testers were active yesterday."
- "Pull the campaign report and draft my production access answers from the real numbers."

The main tool is get_testers: it adds the app, opens its test and returns the steps only a human can do, such as adding the testers' Google Group in Play Console. The agent cannot pay or click Apply for production for you.

### No MCP? Use the HTTP API

POST https://vvrlxzbngxfxddywidoq.supabase.co/rest/v1/rpc/agent_call with the public apikey header listed at https://testerexchange.com/agents/ and the body {"p_token":"tx_YOUR_TOKEN","p_action":"get_testers","p_args":{"package_name":"com.example.app"}}. The schema is at https://testerexchange.com/openapi.json. More tools: https://testerexchange.com/guide/ai-builders/.

### Frequently asked questions

**Can VS Code + Copilot complete the 14-day test for me?** No. The 14 days need real people using your app on their own Android phones. VS Code + Copilot can build the app and drive the setup.

**Is Tester Exchange an official VS Code + Copilot integration?** No. It is an independent service that works with any client supporting remote MCP over HTTP, which VS Code + Copilot does.

**Where does the AAB go?** Upload it to a closed testing release in Play Console, then add your testers' Google Group or email list on that track.

**Is there a free way to get the 12 testers?** Yes. Test other developers' apps at https://testerexchange.com/earn; each app you test brings a tester to yours.

---

{"mcpServers":{"tester-exchange":{"serverUrl":"https://vvrlxzbngxfxddywidoq.supabase.co/functions/v1/mcp","headers":{"Authorization":"Bearer tx_YOUR_TOKEN"}}}}

Replace tx_YOUR_TOKEN with your key and reload Windsurf if the tools do not appear. The server is plain MCP over Streamable HTTP without OAuth; the public tools (about, pricing, platform_stats) work without a key.

The schema is at https://testerexchange.com/openapi.json. More tools: https://testerexchange.com/guide/ai-builders/.

## Get free Google Play testers by testing other developers' apps
URL: https://testerexchange.com/guide/get-free-testers-by-testing-apps/

Google Play makes new personal developer accounts run a closed test with at least 12 testers who stay opted in for 14 days in a row. If you can't pay for testers, you can earn them: test other developers' apps from your Android phone, and they test yours. This guide shows exactly how the credits add up, how long it takes, and how to get your testers sooner.

### The rule you need to meet

Google's Play Console Help says personal developer accounts created after 13 November 2023 must run a closed test with at least 12 testers who have been opted in continuously for at least 14 days before they can apply for production access (https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/14151465).

Other developers have the same problem, so testing each other's apps works: every developer on Tester Exchange needs testers, and every one of them can be a tester.

### How the credits work

- You earn 1 credit for each day you open an app you're testing for at least 30 seconds.
- One tester costs 15 credits: 14 tester-days plus a feedback bonus.
- 12 testers cost 180 credits, 15 testers cost 225. Asking for 14–15 is safer, because some testers drop out.
- New members start with 14 credits (the first 500 members get 90).
- Credits are held, not spent upfront: a tester is paid only for the days they open your app, and unused credits go back to your balance.

### How long it takes

Each app takes about a minute a day, and you can test several apps at the same time. If you open 12 apps a day, you earn 12 credits a day: with the 14 credits you start with, that's 180 credits, enough for 12 testers, in about 14 days. Open fewer apps and it takes longer; how many apps you get each day depends on how many need testers.

You don't have to wait until you have 180: testers you bring yourself through your app's share page don't cost credits, so you only need credits for the seats they don't fill.

### Get your testers sooner: keep testing

- Owners who test go first. Apps whose owners opened at least 3 other apps today or yesterday get testers before apps whose owners don't test.
- Free apps get new testers only while their owner is testing. If you stop opening other apps, your app stops moving up the queue.
- A minute a day is enough. Open the apps on your list, keep each one open for 30 seconds, and come back tomorrow.

### Earn faster: invite people

Every app has a share page. Post its link where you already ask for testers. Each person who joins through your link and completes a test day earns you 30 bonus credits, which is two testers, and they can test your app right away.

### Step by step

1. Set up your closed test in Play Console and keep the opt-in link handy.
2. On your Android phone, open https://testerexchange.com/earn in the browser and sign in with the Google Account your Play Store uses.
3. Tap the green button to join the first app's test, install it from Google Play, and open it for 30 seconds. Come back and repeat for the next app.
4. Add your own app and share its page with anyone who might help.
5. Do this every day. When you have enough credits, start your campaign; keep testing so your app stays near the front.
6. After 14 days with 12 or more testers opted in, apply for production access in Play Console.

### Fair-play rules

- Your own real phone. No emulators, cloud phones or device farms.
- One account per person. Extra accounts are removed.
- Really use the app. Look at a different screen each day and send feedback if something breaks.
- Stay for the full 14 days. Leaving early hurts the developer, the same way it would hurt you.

### Frequently asked questions

**Is it really free?** Yes. You pay with your time: about a minute a day per app you test. Paying is optional and only makes it faster.

**How many credits do I need for 12 testers?** 180 credits: 15 per tester (14 days plus a feedback bonus). 15 testers need 225.

**How long does it take to earn them?** About 14 days if you open 12 apps a day, counting the 14 credits you start with. Invites make it faster: each invited person who completes a test day earns you 30 credits.

**Do I need an Android phone?** Yes. These are Google Play closed tests, so you test on an Android phone signed in to the Google Account your Play Store uses.

**What if I stop testing?** You keep the credits you earned, but a free app gets new testers only while its owner is testing, so your test slows down.

---

## Google Group or email list for your closed test?
URL: https://testerexchange.com/guide/google-group-vs-email-list/

Every closed testing track needs a list of who may install the app. Play Console gives you two options: an email list you manage in Play Console, or a Google Group. Both work for the 12-tester requirement. The difference is how much work it is to add people.

### Quick comparison

- Google Group: anyone with the group link can join, so you don't have to add people one by one. Best when testers come from many places.
- Email list: you paste each tester's Google account email into Play Console. Full control over who gets in, but you have to keep it updated as people join.

### Set up a Google Group

1. Go to groups.google.com and create a group. Set "Who can join" to anyone on the web, so testers don't wait for approval.
2. In Play Console → Testing → Closed testing → your track → Testers, choose Google Groups and add the group's email address.
3. Share two links with testers: the group link (join first) and the opt-in link (become a tester).
4. Testers install the app from Google Play with the same Google account they used to join the group.

### Set up an email list

1. In Play Console → Testing → Closed testing → your track → Testers, create an email list.
2. Paste the Google account emails of your testers, separated by commas, and save.
3. Share the opt-in link. Testers must open it while signed in with the email you added.

### Mistakes that stop testers from seeing your app

- The tester joined with one Google account but their phone's Play Store uses another.
- The group requires approval, so testers are stuck waiting.
- The tester joined the group but never opened the opt-in link and tapped "Become a tester".
- The release isn't approved yet. Testers can't install until the closed track is live.

### Frequently asked questions

**Do group members count toward the 12 testers?** Only people who opted in through the opt-in link count, whichever list type you use.

**Can I use both?** Yes. A track can have email lists and Google Groups at the same time.

**Can testers stay anonymous?** With a Google Group you never need to collect emails yourself. With an email list you need each tester's Google account email.

---

## Getting 12 testers for Google Play in Africa
URL: https://testerexchange.com/guide/google-play-12-testers-africa/

If you build Android apps in Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana, South Africa, Egypt, Ethiopia or anywhere else in Africa and opened a personal Google Play developer account after 13 November 2023, Google will not let you publish to production until you run a closed test with at least 12 testers opted in for 14 days in a row. This guide explains the rule in plain words and shows the cheapest ways to meet it, including a free route that needs only an Android phone and a browser.

### The rule, in plain words

Google Play Console Help says personal developer accounts created after 13 November 2023 must run a closed test with a minimum of 12 testers who have been opted in continuously for at least 14 days before they can apply for production access. The rule is the same in every country: there is no different version for Africa.

Each tester's 14 days start when that person opts in. If someone opts out, their count starts again.

### Why it is hard for many developers

- Your circle may not have 12 Android users who will keep going. Friends often install once and forget, or opt out by accident.
- Testers must have a Google account on an Android phone and join your test through a Google Group or an email list you add in Play Console.
- Engagement matters. Google lists insufficient tester engagement as a reason you may need to keep testing, so 12 people who never open the app is a risk.
- Paying abroad can be awkward. If an international card payment does not go through, you need another way to pay, or a free route.

### The free route: test other apps, get testers back

1. On your Android phone, open https://testerexchange.com/earn in the browser and sign in with Google. No extra app is needed.
2. Add your app and the closed testing group. Tester Exchange can connect to Google Play and add its testers group to your track, or you add it by hand in Play Console under Closed testing, Testers.
3. Each day, tap the apps on your list and open each one. It takes about a minute a day.
4. Every app you test brings a tester to yours. Each day testers open your app is recorded, and dropouts are replaced automatically.

### The paid route: pay once, test nothing

If you would rather not test other apps, pay once on https://testerexchange.com/ and paid apps get testers first. Prices are shown in your own currency. You can pay by card, Google Pay, Apple Pay or PayPal, or with USDT or USDC on BNB Chain, Polygon, Arbitrum or Base sent straight to the Tester Exchange wallet with no fee. Purchases are final.

### Applying for production

1. Wait until 12 testers have each passed 14 consecutive opted-in days. Count from the day your 12th tester joined.
2. Open the Dashboard in Play Console and click Apply for production.
3. Answer the questions about your closed test, your app and your production readiness. Describe the feedback you collected and what you changed.
4. Google says review usually takes seven days or less.

### Tips that save time

- Aim for 15 testers, not 12, so one dropout does not push your date back.
- Ship a small update during the 14 days so testers have a reason to open the app again.
- If your app needs a local phone number or works only in one country, say so in the app's test notes, or testers elsewhere may not get past the login screen.
- Keep your closed test running until production access is approved.

### Frequently asked questions

**Is the 12 testers rule different in Nigeria or Kenya?** No. Google applies the same rule to personal developer accounts created after 13 November 2023 in every country.

**Do testers have to live in my country?** No. Testers can be anywhere, as long as your closed test is available in their country and the app works for them.

**Can I do this with only a phone?** Yes. The free route works in your Android phone's browser at https://testerexchange.com/earn.

**Can I earn money testing apps?** Some apps on Tester Exchange pay cash to testers who finish all 14 days. You can cash out to PayPal, Binance Pay or Payoneer.

**How long until I can publish?** At least 14 days after your 12th tester opts in, plus Google's review, which usually takes seven days or less.

---

This guide explains the rule simply, then shows a free route that needs only an Android phone and a browser, and a paid route with payment methods that work in China.

### The rule, in plain words

Google Play Console Help says personal developer accounts created after 13 November 2023 must run a closed test with a minimum of 12 testers who have been opted in continuously for at least 14 days before they can apply for production access. The rule is the same in China as everywhere else.

Each tester's 14 days start when that person opts in. If someone opts out and rejoins, their count starts again.

### Why swap groups often fail

- Nobody can see who really tested. In WeChat and QQ closed-testing swap groups, members post screenshots, but a screenshot does not show that someone kept the app for 14 days.
- People drop out. When one tester leaves, your 14 days can move back.
- Engagement matters. Google lists insufficient tester engagement as a reason you may need to keep testing, so installs alone are a risk.
- It takes hours. Testing many apps by hand every day to earn 12 testers back is a lot of work.

### The free route: test other apps, get testers back

1. On your Android phone, open https://testerexchange.com/earn in the browser and sign in with Google. No extra app is needed.
2. Add your app. Tester Exchange can connect to Google Play and add its testers group to your closed testing track, or you add it by hand in Play Console under Closed testing, Testers.
3. Each day, tap the apps on your list and open each one. It takes about a minute a day.
4. Every app you test brings a tester to yours. Each day testers open your app is recorded, and dropouts are replaced automatically.

### The paid route: pay once, test nothing

If you would rather not test other apps, pay once on https://testerexchange.com/ and paid apps get testers first. On the site prices are shown in yuan. At checkout you can pay with Alipay, WeChat Pay or a UnionPay card, as well as other cards and PayPal. Purchases are final.

### Applying for production

1. Wait until 12 testers have each passed 14 consecutive opted-in days. Count from the day your 12th tester joined.
2. Open the Dashboard in Play Console and click Apply for production.
3. Answer the questions about your closed test, your app and your production readiness. Describe the feedback you collected and what you changed.
4. Google says review usually takes seven days or less.

### Tips that save time

- Aim for 15 testers, not 12, so one dropout does not push your date back.
- Ship a small update during the 14 days so testers have a reason to open the app again.
- If your app needs a Chinese phone number or a login that needs services blocked outside China to log in, add a test login in the test notes, or testers elsewhere may not get past the first screen.
- Keep your closed test running until production access is approved.

### Frequently asked questions

**Is the 12 testers rule different in China?** No. Google applies the same rule to personal developer accounts created after 13 November 2023 in every country.

**Can I pay with Alipay or WeChat Pay?** Yes. Alipay, WeChat Pay and UnionPay cards are offered at checkout.

**Do testers have to be in China?** No. Testers can be anywhere, as long as your closed test is available in their country and the app works for them.

**Can I do this with only a phone?** Yes. The free route works in your Android phone's browser at https://testerexchange.com/earn.

**How long until I can publish?** At least 14 days after your 12th tester opts in, plus Google's review, which usually takes seven days or less.

---

India has one of the largest Android developer communities in the world, and many first-time developers, students and App Inventor or Kodular builders hit this rule. This guide explains it simply and shows a free route and a paid route.

### The rule, in plain words

Google Play Console Help says personal developer accounts created after 13 November 2023 must run a closed test with a minimum of 12 testers who have been opted in continuously for at least 14 days before they can apply for production access. The rule is the same in India as everywhere else.

Each tester's 14 days start when that person opts in. If someone opts out and rejoins, their count starts again.

### Why WhatsApp and Telegram swap groups often fail

- Nobody can see who really tested. Members post screenshots, but a screenshot does not show that someone kept the app for 14 days.
- People drop out. When one tester leaves, your 14 days can move back.
- Engagement matters. Google lists insufficient tester engagement as a reason you may need to keep testing, so installs alone are a risk.
- It takes hours. Testing 20 apps by hand every day to earn 12 testers back is a lot of work.

### The free route: test other apps, get testers back

### The paid route: pay once with UPI or card, test nothing

### Applying for production

2. Open the Dashboard in Play Console and click Apply for production.
3. Answer the questions about your closed test, your app and your production readiness. Describe the feedback you collected and what you changed.

### Tips for students and first-time developers

### Frequently asked questions

**Can I pay with UPI?** Yes. Checkout offers local methods such as UPI, and prices are shown in your own currency.

**I built my app with App Inventor or Kodular. Does this work?** Yes. The rule and the steps are the same for any Android app published through Play Console.

**How long until I can publish?** At least 14 days after your 12th tester opts in, plus Google's review, which usually takes seven days or less.

- Engagement matters. Google lists insufficient tester engagement as a reason you may need to keep testing, so installs alone are a risk.
- It takes hours. Testing many apps by hand every day to earn 12 testers back is a lot of work.

### The free route: test other apps, get testers back

1. On your Android phone, open https://testerexchange.com/earn in the browser and sign in with Google. No extra app is needed.
2. Add your app. Tester Exchange can connect to Google Play and add its testers group to your closed testing track, or you add it by hand in Play Console under Closed testing, Testers.
3. Each day, tap the apps on your list and open each one. It takes about a minute a day.
4. Every app you test brings a tester to yours. Each day testers open your app is recorded, and dropouts are replaced automatically.

### The paid route: pay once, test nothing

If you would rather not test other apps, pay once on https://testerexchange.com/ and paid apps get testers first. Prices are shown in your currency. You can pay by card (Visa, Mastercard and more), Google Pay or Apple Pay, or with USDT or USDC sent straight to the Tester Exchange wallet with no fee. In Brazil you can also pay with Pix. OXXO and Mercado Pago are not available at checkout yet.

### Applying for production

1. Wait until 12 testers have each passed 14 consecutive opted-in days. Count from the day your 12th tester joined.
2. Open the Dashboard in Play Console and click Apply for production.
3. Answer the questions about your closed test, your app and your production readiness. Describe the feedback you collected and what you changed.
4. Google says review usually takes seven days or less.

### Tips that save time

- Aim for 15 testers, not 12, so one dropout does not push your date back.
- Ship a small update during the 14 days so testers have a reason to open the app again.
- If your app needs a local phone number or OTP to log in, add a test login in the test notes, or testers elsewhere may not get past the first screen.
- Keep your closed test running until production access is approved.

### Frequently asked questions

**Is the 12 testers rule different in Mexico and Latin America?** No. Google applies the same rule to personal developer accounts created after 13 November 2023 in every country.

**Can I pay with OXXO or Mercado Pago?** Not yet. You can pay by card, Google Pay, Apple Pay or USDT/USDC, or use the free route at https://testerexchange.com/earn.

**Do testers have to be in Mexico and Latin America?** No. Testers can be anywhere, as long as your closed test is available in their country and the app works for them.

**Can I do this with only a phone?** Yes. The free route works in your Android phone's browser at https://testerexchange.com/earn.

**How long until I can publish?** At least 14 days after your 12th tester opts in, plus Google's review, which usually takes seven days or less.
